neighbours.label: The main verb of a news headline whose subject is a bare noun phrase (no article), vs the same news told as an ordinary prose sentence

quiet:
Business briefs
The local bakery announced last week that it had won a contract with the city schools.

Tech roundup
A spokesperson for the chipmaker described the new processor at a press event.

Health news
In a large study, researchers looked at coffee drinking and liver disease.

Racing notes
The trainer said that the colt had looked well on the gallops this week.

Energy briefs
After the turbine upgrade, engineers measured the output of the wind farm.

Science roundup
Divers have often watched octopuses carrying coconut shells across the sand.

Retail briefs

predictions: Fire items 0.2-0.5 on the headline verb; prose near misses under 0.1.
notes: Card: verbs after title-like subjects ('Whale uses', 'APD utilizes', 'Eco-truck reduces', 'gelding is getting'). Probe: 'Solar startup raises funds' 0.517, 'Bacteria uses magnetic crystals' 0.218, 'New router offers' 0.227, 'Late-blooming filly is finding' 0.408; prose 'The solar startup said on Monday' 0.071, 'Our neighbour uses the garden shed' 0.042.
